stance_text: Watch — unchanged, bias now neutral; contracts and pricing improved, but delivery slipped, the new GPU debt costs over 10%, and about 486 million shares are already outstanding or committed
lens_text: FY2030 (June 2030) adjusted EBITDA x exit EV/EBITDA (5.5x/6.5x/8.0x, one turn below October because new GPU debt costs 10.4-10.7%), less end-2029 net debt, over end-2029 shares starting from about 486M outstanding or committed; three-year value, undiscounted

bear.basis: Build stops near 0.6GW at $11.7M per MW (10% below today's blended $13.3M): FY2030 revenue $7.0B at 50% EBITDA margin ($3.5B) x 5.5x = $19.25B, less $18B net debt (about $13.4B more, against $18.9B of partly cancellable commitments; 2029/2030 notes repaid), on 700M shares

base.basis: >$4B ARR by early 2027, about 0.8GW by end-2027 and about 1.0GW billed in FY2030 at $13.0M per MW: revenue $13.0B at 58% ($7.54B) x 6.5x = $49.0B, less $33.56B net debt, on 630M shares (486M outstanding or committed, about 114M more issued, and 29.7M from the 2029/2030 notes converting; 2031-2033 notes stay debt)

bull.basis: About 1.3GW billed at $14.2M per MW: revenue $18.5B at 63% ($11.66B) x 8.0x = $93.2B, less $39.56B net debt after all convertible notes convert (about 127M shares), on 652M shares

horizon_text: End-2029 value on forward (FY2030) adjusted EBITDA, undiscounted
thesis: Q1 FY2027 improved the contracts and worsened the funding: backlog rose 22% to $20.3B (two-thirds investment grade) and new contract pricing rose 11-12%, but the >$4B ARR target moved from year-end 2026 to January-February 2027, the new GPU debt costs 10.4-10.7% effectively, and about 486M shares are already outstanding or committed. At that debt cost the base case earns about nothing on FY2030 normalized earnings, so its $24.54 value rests on the multiple the market pays for growing EBITDA.
consensus_view: No current Street snapshot was captured; the October call recorded a $75.42 mean target. The stock fell from $23.95 to $19.73 in eleven days, at an enterprise value of about 3.2x the >$4B ARR target, as the neocloud group sold off on funding costs.
variant_view: We sit between the October Street targets and the price. The Street mean of $75.42 looks to ignore the dilution already committed (about 486M shares) and debt now costing over 10%; the price looks to ignore that two-thirds of a $20.3B backlog is investment grade and new contracts carry prepayments of up to 90% of GPU capex. The checkable tests are the >$4B ARR operating by the end of February 2027 and at least $2B of data center financing closed by June 30, 2027.

Base FY2030 pre-tax normalized earnings are about -$0.7B (depreciation about 38% of revenue, stock compensation 3%, interest blended about 8.7% on $33.6B with secured debt at 10.5%), so the base value rests on the multiple paid for growing EBITDA (18.9x FY2030 EBIT).
capital.multiples gives no usable peers: IREN's SIC code (6199) is from its mining years.

First review round (C; evidence 3, valuation 2, variant view 3, risk 3, calibration 2): share paths ignored about 62M of RSUs and Investment Rights and convert shares in the bull, the bear priced capacity above the base, the new GPU debt's 10.4-10.7% effective cost was missed, kill criteria missed the bear's dilution path, and the value change was misattributed. First draft: Own, $6.15 / $40.27 / $117.44 at 30/50/20 on 6.0x/7.5x/9.0x, fair value $45.47.

Second review round (B; evidence 3, valuation 3, variant view 4, risk 3, calibration 3): convert shares (2029/2030 notes convert in the base; 2031-2033 notes are about 97.5M shares, not 115M), net debt on a September 30 basis, the interest blend at the 10.5% secured rate, mostly out-of-the-money options removed from committed shares, and kill-criteria thresholds. Second-draft values were $1.79 / $25.02 / $83.19, fair value $25.61.

low_score_reasons: evidence: end-2029 net debt and share paths have no schedule; the 30M Investment Rights' terms are not in the saved sources; the bull's conversion shares did not match Note 22 and the conversion prices.

valuation: the base equity exists only because 6.5x EBITDA (18.9x EBIT) is applied to a business whose EBIT yield on EV (5.3%) is below its blended debt cost; the one-turn multiple cut is a judgment; the base ignored the $445M of 2029/2030 notes whose trigger is met.
risk: the funding kill criterion had no dollar threshold and the customer criterion differed between the note and call.json.
calibration: all three revenue paths sit above the 99.9th percentile of their bucket; 0.75 on Q2 AI Cloud revenue of at least $250M was high given ARR-to-revenue lags.
review.counter_case: The equity has no earnings at the end of the horizon. Base FY2030 EBIT of $2.6B is 5.3% of a $49B EV, against a 7.4% blended debt cost and 10.4-10.7% on this quarter's GPU debt. Valuing EBIT to earn the blended debt cost leaves the base equity at about $1.89 a share, and at a 9% secured yield at nothing. The $25 base is a bet that in 2029 the market pays 18.9x EBIT for a business that has not yet earned its interest. With convert dilution, 486M shares outstanding or committed before the $6B gap is funded, and a 35% bear at $1.79, the expected return is closer to Avoid than to Watch.
review.response: Accepted the corrections: the 2029/2030 notes now convert in the base (630M shares, $33.56B net debt, $24.54) and all notes convert in the bull (652M shares, $82.31); net debt and EV are on a September 30 basis; the interest blend uses 10.5% on secured debt, giving about -$0.7B of base FY2030 pre-tax earnings; options are dropped from committed shares and the Investment Rights are stated as an assumption; the funding criterion fires below $3B committed and the customer criterion is $100M of backlog in both files; the Q2 AI Cloud claim is 0.65. The fair value is $25.24, 8.6% a year, Watch. On the counter-case: valuing the 2029 equity on EBIT at the debt yield treats a business still growing about 25% a year as if it were mature; the market prices growing infrastructure on EBITDA, which is why the call uses lower multiples rather than an earnings yield, and why the bear at $1.79 carries 35%. The call stays Watch rather than Avoid because the contracted backlog is two-thirds investment grade and the base, on these harsher terms, still returns 7.5% a year; the kill criteria on dilution, funding and Microsoft fees are where the Avoid case would show first.
